findings.title: Service layer is largely untested
findings.what: 12 test files cover 84 source files (0.14 file ratio); the service + api layers have almost no tests.
findings.why: Untested business logic regresses silently on every refactor -- the cost lands on the next change, not this one.
findings.how: Add characterization tests for the 3 busiest services first, then gate the CI step you already have on a minimum ratio.

findings.title: Unescaped HTML sink on user-influenced content
findings.what: 3 dangerouslySetInnerHTML usages render content that can carry user input.
findings.why: That is the classic stored-XSS surface -- one unescaped field is enough.
findings.how: Sanitize at the render boundary (an allowlist HTML sanitizer) or switch to text rendering where markup is not required.

findings.title: Errors swallowed in the HTTP layer
findings.what: 4 empty catch blocks discard fetch failures with no log, no rethrow, no user signal.
findings.why: A swallowed failure looks like success until the data is wrong downstream -- the hardest class of bug to trace.
findings.how: In each catch, at minimum log with context and rethrow (or return a typed error result) so the failure is visible.

findings.title: N+1 fetch on the report endpoint
findings.what: A fetch runs inside a per-row loop (plus 5 await-in-loop sites) when building the report response.
findings.why: Latency scales linearly with row count -- fine at 10 rows, a timeout at 10,000.
findings.how: Batch the per-row fetch into a single query/request outside the loop, then map results in memory.
